chapter.name: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round
chapter.blurb: Circles, chords, the circumcircle, angles subtended by arcs, and cyclic quadrilaterals.

scope_in.item: Definition of a circle, radius, chord, diameter, locus and the symmetries of a circle
Circles through two points and the unique circle through three non-collinear points; circumcircle and circumcentre
Equal chords and equal angles at the centre; the perpendicular from the centre to a chord
Distance of a chord from the centre; the longer chord is closer; chord length from radius and distance
Angle subtended by an arc at the centre and at the circle; angle in a semicircle
Concyclic points and cyclic quadrilaterals: opposite angles and converse
End-of-chapter problems on chords, arcs and cyclic quadrilaterals

scope_out.item: Tangents to a circle and the tangent-radius theorem
scope_out.reason: The text says next year brings many more circle results

scope_out.item: Circumference, area and arc length of a circle
Alternate segment theorem and intersecting chord products

concepts.name: Circles: definitions and symmetries
concepts.description: A circle as a locus of points at a fixed distance from a centre, radius, chord, diameter, and the reflection and rotation symmetries of a circle.
concepts.idea: Every point of a circle is the same distance from the centre, and this makes the circle perfectly symmetrical.
concepts.rule: A circle is the set (locus) of points in a plane equidistant from a fixed point, the centre. A chord joins two points of the circle; a chord through the centre is a diameter. Every diameter is a line of reflection symmetry, and the circle has rotational symmetry about the centre through any angle.
concepts.example: A circle of radius 5 has diameter 10, the longest chord.

questions.q: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are
questions.a: at the same distance from a fixed point
o: at the same distance from a fixed point
at the same distance from a fixed line in the plane
on a straight line passing through a fixed point
inside a square with a fixed centre point

questions.q: A chord that passes through the centre of a circle is called a
questions.a: diameter

questions.q: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on it is the ____.
questions.a: radius

questions.q: The set of all points that satisfy a given condition is called a
questions.a: locus

questions.q: A circle has reflection symmetry across
questions.a: every diameter

questions.q: A circle has rotational symmetry
questions.a: about its centre through any angle
o: about its centre through any angle
only through 90 degrees, like a square, about its centre
only through 180 degrees, like a rectangle, about its centre
about no point, since a circle has only reflection symmetry

questions.q: The longest chord of a circle is
questions.a: a diameter

questions.q: The longest chord in a circle of radius 5 units has length
questions.a: 10 units

questions.q: Explain why a rotating wheel looks the same at all times.
questions.a: A circle has complete rotational symmetry: rotating it about its centre through any angle leaves it looking exactly the same, so you cannot tell which point is which.
s: Refers to rotational symmetry of the circle about its centre
Says rotation through any angle gives the same shape

questions.q: A circle has radius 6 cm. Its diameter is
questions.a: 12 cm

questions.q: All ____ of a circle are lines of reflection symmetry.
questions.a: diameters

questions.q: The locus of points equidistant from two points A and B is
questions.a: the perpendicular bisector of AB
o: a circle through A and B
the line through A parallel to B

questions.q: Describe how folding a circular piece of paper can locate its centre.
questions.a: Fold the circle so the boundaries overlap and open it; the crease is a diameter. Fold again in another direction to get a second diameter. The centre is where the two creases meet.
s: Folds so boundaries overlap to get a crease (a diameter)
A second fold gives another diameter; the centre is where they meet

questions.q: How many lines of reflection symmetry does (i) a square and (ii) a regular hexagon have?
questions.a: (i) 4 lines, (ii) 6 lines.
s: Square has 4
Regular hexagon has 6

questions.q: All points in a plane are 3 cm from a fixed point O. Describe the locus, name the radius and give the length of the longest chord.
questions.a: The locus is a circle with centre O. Its radius is 3 cm and the longest chord is the diameter, 6 cm.
s: Locus is a circle centred at O
Radius 3 cm
Longest chord (diameter) 6 cm

questions.q: Which statement is true for every circle?
questions.a: All points on it are at equal distance from the centre
o: All points on it are at equal distance from the centre
Only some points are at equal distance from the centre
It has exactly one line of symmetry
Its longest chord is a radius

questions.q: Is there a smallest chord in a circle? Explain.
questions.a: No. As a chord is pushed towards the boundary it gets shorter and shorter and finally becomes a single point of length zero, so there is no smallest positive chord.
s: Chords can get arbitrarily short as they move to the boundary
Length shrinks to zero at a single point

questions.q: Explain why the perpendicular bisector of AB is the locus of points equidistant from A and B.
questions.a: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from A and B. Conversely, every point equidistant from A and B lies on that bisector. Both directions hold, so it is exactly the locus.
s: Every point on the bisector is equidistant from A and B
Every equidistant point lies on the bisector
Concludes it is the locus

questions.q: Ria says a circle has only one line of reflection symmetry. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. Every diameter is a line of reflection symmetry, and a circle has infinitely many diameters.
s: States she is wrong
Every diameter is a line of symmetry, infinitely many

questions.q: Describe how to find the centre of a circle by drawing two chords and explain why your method works.
questions.a: Draw two non-parallel chords and construct their perpendicular bisectors. The centre is equidistant from the ends of each chord, so it lies on both bisectors, and they meet at the centre.
s: Draws two chords and their perpendicular bisectors
Centre lies on each bisector because it is equidistant from the chord ends
The bisectors meet at the centre

concepts.name: Circles through two and three points; the circumcircle
concepts.description: How many circles pass through two points, and the unique circle through three non-collinear points: circumcircle and circumcentre.
concepts.idea: The centre of a circle through A and B is equidistant from them, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
concepts.rule: Infinitely many circles pass through two points, with centres on their perpendicular bisector. Three non-collinear points lie on exactly one circle (Theorem 1), centred at the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors. Circumcentre: inside for an acute triangle, outside for an obtuse triangle, at the midpoint of the hypotenuse for a right triangle.
concepts.example: For a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 cm the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse and the circumradius is 5 cm.

questions.q: The number of circles that pass through two given points is
questions.a: infinitely many

questions.q: The number of circles through three non-collinear points is
questions.a: exactly one

questions.q: The centre of the circle passing through the vertices of a triangle is called the ____.
questions.a: circumcentre

questions.q: The centres of all circles through A and B lie on
questions.a: the perpendicular bisector of AB
o: the line through A parallel to B

questions.q: The circle passing through all three vertices of a triangle is its
questions.a: circumcircle

questions.q: For an acute-angled triangle the circumcentre lies
questions.a: inside the triangle

questions.q: For a right-angled triangle the circumcentre lies at
questions.a: the midpoint of the hypotenuse
o: the right-angled vertex, where the two legs meet
the midpoint of one of the legs of the triangle
outside the triangle, on the side opposite the hypotenuse

questions.q: For an obtuse-angled triangle the circumcentre lies
questions.a: outside the triangle
o: at the midpoint of the longest side

questions.q: Why is there no circle through three collinear points?
questions.a: The perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC are parallel when A, B, C are collinear, so they never meet. There is no point equidistant from all three to serve as a centre.
s: The perpendicular bisectors are parallel
So no common centre exists

questions.q: The smallest circle through A and B has a radius equal to
questions.a: half the length of AB

questions.q: If AB = 10 cm, the least possible radius of a circle through A and B is ____ cm.
The circumcentre of a triangle is found as the intersection of
questions.a: the perpendicular bisectors of two sides
o: the perpendicular bisectors of two sides
the angle bisectors of the three angles of the triangle
the medians drawn from the vertices to the opposite sides
the altitudes drawn from the vertices, and only the altitudes

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the radius of its circumcircle.
questions.a: Hypotenuse = 10 cm. The circumcentre is its midpoint, so the radius is 5 cm.
s: Hypotenuse 10 cm
Circumradius 5 cm

questions.q: State the position of the circumcentre for (i) an acute triangle, (ii) an obtuse triangle.
questions.a: (i) inside the triangle; (ii) outside the triangle.
s: Acute: inside
Obtuse: outside

questions.q: Describe how to draw the circle through three non-collinear points A, B and C.
questions.a: Draw the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC. They meet at a point O. With centre O and radius OA draw a circle; it passes through A, B and C.
s: Perpendicular bisectors of two sides drawn
Their intersection O is the centre
Radius OA gives the circle through all three points

questions.q: Moving away from segment AB along its perpendicular bisector, the radii of the circles through A and B
questions.a: increase

questions.q: Explain why the circumcentre of an obtuse-angled triangle lies outside the triangle.
questions.a: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at the circumcentre. For an obtuse triangle they meet outside because the circle through the vertices has the longest side as a chord that is not a diameter, and the centre lies on the far side of it from the obtuse vertex.
s: States the circumcentre is where the bisectors meet
Explains it falls outside because of the obtuse angle

questions.q: Show that exactly one circle passes through three non-collinear points A, B and C.
questions.a: A centre O must satisfy OA = OB and OA = OC, so O is on the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC. These lines are not parallel since A, B, C are not collinear, so they meet in exactly one point. That point O is the only centre and the radius OA is fixed.
s: O lies on both perpendicular bisectors
The bisectors are not parallel so meet at exactly one point
So the centre and radius, and hence the circle, are unique

questions.q: Sam says two points A and B lie on exactly one circle. Evaluate.
questions.a: He is wrong. Any point on the perpendicular bisector of AB can be the centre of a circle through A and B, so there are infinitely many.
s: States he is wrong
Centres can be any point of the perpendicular bisector

questions.q: Find the centre and radius of the circle through P (0, 0), Q (4, 0) and R (0, 3), and explain how you know.
questions.a: The triangle is right-angled at P (the axes are perpendicular), so the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse QR, which is (2, 1.5). QR = 5 so the radius is 2.5.
s: Recognises the right angle at P
Centre is the midpoint of QR, (2, 1.5)
Radius 2.5

concepts.name: Chords and angles at the centre; the perpendicular from the centre
concepts.description: Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre and conversely; the line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it and conversely.
concepts.idea: Triangles made from two radii and a chord are isosceles, and congruence of these triangles gives the chord theorems.
concepts.rule: Theorem 2: equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre (SSS). Theorem 3: chords subtending equal angles at the centre are equal (SAS). Theorem 4: the line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord. Theorem 5: the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it.
concepts.example: If chords AB and DE are equal and angle ACB = 54 degrees then angle DCE = 54 degrees.

questions.q: Equal chords of a circle subtend
questions.a: equal angles at the centre

questions.q: Chords that subtend equal angles at the centre are
questions.a: equal in length

questions.q: The line from the centre of a circle to the midpoint of a chord is ____ to the chord.
questions.a: perpendicular

questions.q: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord
questions.a: bisects the chord
o: is always a radius of length 0

questions.q: Theorem 2 (equal chords subtend equal angles) is proved using which congruence rule?
questions.a: SSS

questions.q: Theorem 3 (equal angles at the centre give equal chords) is proved using which congruence rule?
questions.a: SAS

questions.q: The triangle formed by a chord and the centre of the circle is
questions.a: isosceles

questions.q: In the proof of Theorem 4, angles CMA and CMB are equal and lie on a line, so each is
questions.a: 90 degrees

questions.q: Show that the triangle formed by a chord AB and the centre C is isosceles.
questions.a: CA and CB are both radii of the circle, so CA = CB. A triangle with two equal sides is isosceles.
s: CA and CB are radii
So CA = CB and the triangle is isosceles

questions.q: Chords AB and DE of a circle with centre C are equal and angle ACB = 54 degrees. Then angle DCE is
questions.a: 54 degrees

questions.q: A chord subtends 70 degrees at the centre. An equal chord subtends ____ degrees at the centre.
M is the midpoint of a chord AB of length 16 cm and CM is perpendicular to AB, C being the centre. Then AM is
questions.a: 8 cm

questions.q: Chords AB and DE of a circle with centre C are equal. Show that angle ACB equals angle DCE.
questions.a: CA = CB = CD = CE (radii) and AB = DE. So triangles CAB and CDE are congruent by SSS, hence angle ACB = angle DCE.
s: Equal radii and AB = DE identified
SSS congruence gives equal angles

questions.q: C is the centre and CM is perpendicular to chord AB at M. Show that AM = BM.
questions.a: CA = CB (radii), CM is common and angle CMA = angle CMB = 90 degrees. By RHS, triangles CMA and CMB are congruent, so AM = BM.
s: RHS: hypotenuses CA = CB, common side CM, right angles
Concludes AM = BM

questions.q: An isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC is inscribed in a circle. Show that the altitude from A to BC passes through the centre.
questions.a: The centre O is equidistant from B and C, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC. In an isosceles triangle the altitude from A to BC is also the perpendicular bisector of BC. Both are the same line, so the altitude passes through O.
s: O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC
In an isosceles triangle the altitude from A is the perpendicular bisector of BC
Hence it passes through O

questions.q: C is the centre of a circle and CM is perpendicular to chord AB. Then M is
questions.a: the midpoint of AB

questions.q: Two chords subtend equal angles at the centre. Are they equal in length? Explain.
questions.a: Yes. The radii to their endpoints are equal and the included angles are equal, so the two triangles are congruent by SAS and the chords (third sides) are equal.
s: Equal radii and equal included angles
SAS gives equal chords

questions.q: Prove that the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre of the circle.
questions.a: For chord AB with centre O, OA = OB (radii). Every point equidistant from A and B lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, so O lies on it.
s: OA = OB because both are radii
Points equidistant from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector
So the bisector passes through O

questions.q: Vikram says two chords that subtend different angles at the centre can still be equal. Evaluate.
questions.a: He is wrong. By Theorem 2 equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, so chords with different central angles are unequal.
s: States he is wrong
Cites that equal chords subtend equal angles

questions.q: Explain how to draw, with a compass, a second chord DE equal to a given chord AB, and why it subtends the same angle at the centre.
questions.a: Set the compass to length AB, place its point on any point D of the circle and mark E on the circle; then DE = AB. Triangles CAB and CDE are congruent by SSS, so the angles at the centre are equal.
s: Compass set to AB and used to mark D and E on the circle
DE = AB
SSS gives equal central angles

concepts.name: Distance of a chord from the centre
concepts.description: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre and conversely; the longer of two chords is closer to the centre; chord length from radius and distance.
concepts.idea: The distance of a chord from the centre is the perpendicular distance; the greater the distance, the shorter the chord.
concepts.rule: Chords of equal length are at equal distance from the centre and conversely (Theorems 6 and 7). The longer chord is closer (Theorem 8). If the perpendicular distance is d and the radius is r, the chord length is 2 x sqrt(r^2 - d^2).
concepts.example: Radius 13 and distance 5 give half-chord sqrt(169 - 25) = 12, so the chord is 24.

questions.q: Chords of equal length in a circle are
questions.a: at the same distance from the centre
o: at the same distance from the centre
at different distances from the centre

questions.q: Chords that are equidistant from the centre of a circle are
questions.a: equal in length

questions.q: Of two unequal chords of a circle, the longer one is ____ to the centre.
questions.a: closer

questions.q: The chord nearest to the centre of a circle is
questions.a: the diameter, at distance 0
o: a chord of length 0 at the very edge of the circle
a radius, since it starts at the centre and ends on the circle
the shortest chord of the circle, lying on its edge

questions.q: The distance of a chord from the centre means
questions.a: the perpendicular distance from the centre to the chord
o: the perpendicular distance from the centre to the chord
the length of the chord itself, measured end to end
the distance from the centre to one end of the chord
the length of the arc cut off by the chord

questions.q: If a chord is longer than another chord, then its distance from the centre is
questions.a: less

questions.q: For a chord at distance d from the centre of a circle of radius r, half the chord length is
questions.a: sqrt(r^2 - d^2)

questions.q: The length of a chord at distance d from the centre of a circle of radius r is
questions.a: 2 sqrt(r^2 - d^2)

questions.q: Explain why the diameter is the longest chord.
questions.a: A diameter passes through the centre, so its distance from the centre is 0, the smallest possible. By Theorem 8 the chord closest to the centre is the longest.
s: Diameter has distance 0 from the centre
The closer a chord, the longer it is (Theorem 8)

questions.q: A chord is 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 13 cm. Its length is
questions.a: 24 cm

questions.q: A chord is 6 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. The chord length is ____ cm.
A circle has diameter 26 cm and a chord of length 24 cm. The distance of the chord from the centre is
questions.a: 5 cm

questions.q: A circle has radius 15 cm and a chord is 9 cm from the centre. Find the length of the chord.
questions.a: Half the chord = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. The chord is 24 cm.
s: Half-chord sqrt(225 - 81) = 12
Chord 24 cm

questions.q: A chord of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre. Find the radius.
questions.a: Half the chord is 8. r^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 = 100, so r = 10 cm.
s: r = 10 cm

questions.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 6 cm and 8 cm are on opposite sides of the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the distance between their midpoints.
questions.a: The 6 cm chord is at sqrt(25 - 9) = 4 cm from the centre. The 8 cm chord is at sqrt(25 - 16) = 3 cm. On opposite sides the distance between the midpoints is 4 + 3 = 7 cm.
s: Distance 4 cm for the 6 cm chord
Distance 3 cm for the 8 cm chord
Opposite sides so 4 + 3 = 7 cm

questions.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 10 cm and 24 cm lie on the same side of the centre, 7 cm apart. The radius is
questions.a: 13 cm

questions.q: The distance of chord AB from the centre is twice the distance of chord CD from the centre. Can we conclude that CD = 2AB? Explain.
questions.a: No. CD is longer than AB because it is closer to the centre, but the length is 2 sqrt(r^2 - d^2), not proportional to d. For r = 5, d = 1 gives 2 sqrt(24) and d = 2 gives 2 sqrt(21), which are not in ratio 2 : 1.
s: CD is longer since it is closer
Not double, with a counter-example or the formula

questions.q: Using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem, show that chords AB and FG of equal length are equidistant from the centre C.
questions.a: With midpoints E and H, CE^2 = r^2 - (AB/2)^2 and CH^2 = r^2 - (FG/2)^2. Since AB = FG, CE^2 = CH^2, so CE = CH.
s: Right triangles CEA and CHF with hypotenuse r
AB = FG gives CE = CH

questions.q: Nisha says a longer chord is farther from the centre of a circle. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. The longer chord is closer to the centre. The diameter, the longest chord, passes through the centre at distance 0.
s: States she is wrong
Longer chords are closer, e.g. diameter at distance 0

questions.q: Find the radius of a circle in which a chord of 6 cm is 3 cm from the centre.
questions.a: Half the chord is 3 cm and the distance is 3 cm. r^2 = 3^2 + 3^2 = 18, so r = 3 sqrt(2) cm (about 4.24 cm).
s: Half-chord 3 cm and distance 3 cm form a right triangle
r = 3 root 2 cm

concepts.name: Angles subtended by an arc; the angle in a semicircle
concepts.description: An arc subtends double the angle at the centre that it subtends at any point on the remaining circle; angles in the same segment are equal; the angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees.
concepts.idea: The angle an arc makes at the centre is twice the angle it makes at any point of the circle outside the arc.
concepts.rule: Theorem 9: angle at the centre = 2 x angle at a point on the circle outside the arc. So angles subtended at points of the same arc are equal. A diameter subtends 90 degrees at any point on the circle.
concepts.example: An arc subtending 70 degrees at the centre subtends 35 degrees at any point on the circle outside the arc.

questions.q: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is
questions.a: double the angle at any point on the remaining circle
o: double the angle at any point on the remaining circle
half the angle at any point on the remaining part of the circle
equal to the angle at any point on the remaining circle
three times the angle at any point on the remaining circle

questions.q: The angle in a semicircle is
questions.a: 90 degrees

questions.q: A diameter subtends an angle of ____ degrees at any point on the circle.
A corollary is
questions.a: a fact that follows immediately from an already proved result
o: a fact that follows immediately from an already proved result
an unproved guess that seems to follow from the diagram
a definition of a term used in a theorem
a special type of chord that passes through the centre

questions.q: An arc subtends 70 degrees at the centre. At a point on the circle outside the arc it subtends
questions.a: 35 degrees

questions.q: Angles subtended by the same arc at points on the circle outside the arc are
questions.a: equal

questions.q: If the angle subtended at the centre is less than 180 degrees, the arc is a
questions.a: minor arc

questions.q: An arc subtends 40 degrees at a point on the circle outside the arc. Its angle at the centre is
questions.a: 80 degrees

questions.q: Explain why the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle is 90 degrees.
questions.a: The diameter subtends a straight angle of 180 degrees at the centre. The angle at a point on the circle is half of this, so it is 90 degrees.
s: Diameter subtends 180 degrees at the centre
Angle at the circle is half, 90 degrees

questions.q: An arc subtends 100 degrees at the centre. The angle it subtends at a point on the circle outside the arc is
questions.a: 50 degrees

questions.q: The angle at the centre is 120 degrees, so the angle at a point on the circle outside the arc is ____ degrees.
In a circle of radius 12 cm, the central angle AOB is 60 degrees. The chord AB has length
questions.a: 12 cm

questions.q: In a circle with centre O and radius 12 cm, angle AOB = 60 degrees. Find the length of chord AB.
questions.a: OA = OB = 12 cm and angle AOB = 60 degrees, so the isosceles triangle OAB is equilateral. AB = 12 cm.
s: Triangle OAB is isosceles with a 60 degree apex angle, hence equilateral
AB = 12 cm

questions.q: AB is a diameter and C is a point on the circle. Find angle ACB and give the reason.
questions.a: Angle ACB = 90 degrees, because the diameter AB subtends 180 degrees at the centre and the angle at the circle is half of that.
s: 90 degrees
Reason: half of the 180 degree central angle

questions.q: An arc subtends 130 degrees at the centre. Find the angle it subtends at a point on the major arc, and the angle at a point on the minor arc.
questions.a: At a point on the major arc: half of 130 = 65 degrees. At a point on the minor arc the arc measured the other way subtends the reflex angle 360 - 130 = 230 degrees at the centre, so the angle is 115 degrees.
s: 65 degrees on the major arc
Uses the reflex angle 230 degrees
115 degrees

questions.q: D and E are points on the same arc of a circle on the same side of chord AB. Then
questions.a: angle ADB = angle AEB

questions.q: In the proof of Theorem 9 where DC extended meets the circle at E on arc AFB, why is angle BCE = 2 angle BDC?
questions.a: Triangle DCB is isosceles (CB = CD) so angle CBD = angle CDB. Angle BCE is an exterior angle of triangle BCD, so it equals angle CBD + angle CDB = 2 angle BDC.
s: Isosceles triangle DCB gives equal base angles
Exterior angle theorem gives 2 angle BDC

questions.q: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with centre O and angle BAC = 40 degrees. Find angle BOC and angle OBC.
questions.a: Angle BOC = 2 x 40 = 80 degrees. OB = OC so triangle OBC is isosceles and angle OBC = (180 - 80)/2 = 50 degrees.
s: Angle BOC = 80 degrees
OB = OC so base angles are equal
Angle OBC = 50 degrees

questions.q: Asha says the angle subtended by an arc at the circle is equal to the angle it subtends at the centre. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. The angle at the centre is double the angle at any point of the circle outside the arc.
s: States she is wrong
Angle at the centre is double the angle on the circle

questions.q: Let AB be a diameter with centre O and C a point on the circle. Using the isosceles triangles OAC and OBC, show that angle ACB = 90 degrees.
questions.a: Let angle OAC = a. Since OA = OC, angle OCA = a. Let angle OBC = b, so angle OCB = b. In triangle ABC, a + b + (a + b) = 180, so a + b = 90. Angle ACB = a + b = 90 degrees.
s: Uses OA = OC = OB for two isosceles triangles
Angle sum of triangle ABC gives 2(a + b) = 180
Angle ACB = a + b = 90 degrees

concepts.name: Concyclic points and cyclic quadrilaterals
concepts.description: When four points lie on a circle, and the property that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180 degrees and its converse.
concepts.idea: Points on one circle are concyclic; a quadrilateral whose vertices are concyclic is cyclic and its opposite angles are supplementary.
concepts.rule: Theorem 10: if AB subtends equal angles at C and D on the same side, then A, B, C, D are concyclic. Theorem 11: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180 degrees. Theorem 12: if two opposite angles of a quadrilateral add to 180 degrees it is cyclic.
concepts.example: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD with angle A = 75 degrees, angle C = 105 degrees.

questions.q: Points that lie on the same circle are called
questions.a: concyclic

questions.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral the opposite angles add up to
questions.a: 180 degrees

questions.q: A quadrilateral whose vertices lie on a circle is called a ____ quadrilateral.
questions.a: cyclic

questions.q: If two opposite angles of a quadrilateral add up to 180 degrees, then the quadrilateral
questions.a: is cyclic

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and angle A = 75 degrees. Then angle C is
questions.a: 105 degrees

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and angle B = 110 degrees. Then angle D is
questions.a: 70 degrees

questions.q: A quadrilateral ABCD has angles A = 80, B = 110, C = 100 and D = 70 degrees. Can it be cyclic?
questions.a: Yes, because each opposite pair adds to 180 degrees
o: Yes, because each opposite pair adds to 180 degrees
No, because the four angles of the quadrilateral are unequal
No, because 80 degrees is not a right angle
Yes, because all four angles add up to 360 degrees

questions.q: Theorem 10 says that if segment AB subtends equal angles at C and D on the same side of AB, then
questions.a: A, B, C and D are concyclic
o: A, B, C and D are concyclic
AB is a diameter, whichever points C and D are
C and D coincide, so the angles at them are equal
AB is parallel to CD, whichever side they lie on

questions.q: Explain why opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180 degrees.
questions.a: Angle BAD is half the reflex angle BOD at the centre and angle BCD is half the angle BOD. Together they are half of a full turn, 360 degrees, which is 180 degrees.
s: Each opposite angle is half the central angle on the arc it subtends
The two central angles make 360 degrees, so the sum is 180

questions.a: 60 square units

questions.q: Angle P = (2x + 10) degrees and angle R = (3x - 20) degrees are opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral. Find x and both angles.
questions.a: (2x + 10) + (3x - 20) = 180 gives 5x = 190 and x = 38. Angle P = 86 degrees and angle R = 94 degrees.
s: Sets the sum equal to 180 and finds x = 38
P = 86 and R = 94 degrees

questions.q: A quadrilateral has opposite angles 100 degrees and 70 degrees. Can it be cyclic? Explain.
questions.a: No. For a cyclic quadrilateral the opposite angles must add up to 180 degrees, but 100 + 70 = 170.
s: States it cannot be cyclic
Reason: the sum is 170, not 180

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and E is a point on the extension of side CD. Show that the exterior angle CDE equals the interior opposite angle ABC.
questions.a: Angle CDE + angle ADC = 180 degrees (linear pair). Also angle ADC + angle ABC = 180 degrees (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral). So angle CDE = angle ABC.
s: Linear pair: CDE + ADC = 180
Cyclic quadrilateral: ADC + ABC = 180
Concludes CDE = ABC

questions.q: Which quadrilateral can always be inscribed in a circle?
questions.a: a rectangle

questions.q: A rectangle is inscribed in a circle. Show that the point where its diagonals meet is the centre.
questions.a: Each angle of the rectangle is 90 degrees, so each diagonal subtends 90 degrees at a vertex on the circle and is therefore a diameter. Two diameters meet at the centre.
s: Each diagonal subtends a right angle so it is a diameter
Diameters meet at the centre, so the diagonal intersection is the centre

questions.q: MNOP is a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle with MN as a diameter. What can you say about angle MOP and angle MNP? Explain.
questions.a: Points N and O lie on the same side of chord MP, so angles MNP and MOP are angles in the same segment and are equal.
s: Identifies that N and O lie on the same side of chord MP
Angles in the same segment are equal
So angle MOP = angle MNP

questions.q: Leela says a parallelogram with angles 70 degrees and 110 degrees can be inscribed in a circle. Evaluate.
questions.a: She is wrong. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so for them to add to 180 degrees each must be 90 degrees. Only a rectangle can be inscribed.
s: States she is wrong
Equal opposite angles summing to 180 forces 90 degrees, so only a rectangle

questions.q: Give all four angles of a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD with angle A = 80 degrees, and check them.
questions.a: For example A = 80, B = 95, C = 100, D = 85 degrees. A + C = 180, B + D = 180 and the total is 360 degrees.
s: Angle C = 100 degrees
B and D add to 180
Total 360 degrees checked
